items.headline: 2 weeks left for Clarity: State of Crypto
items.subheadline: The Senate leaves town in two weeks. Here's what needs to happen for Clarity to advance before then.
items.author: Nikhilesh De

items.headline: The Clarity Act is the most important consumer protection effort in years
items.subheadline: Consumers should not have to wait for another crisis to get the protections they deserve, argues Summer Mersinger, CEO of the Blockchain Association.
items.author: Summer Mersinger

items.headline: AI is destroying the internet. Math is our only hope.
items.subheadline: The rise of autonomous AI agents necessitates the utilization of zero-knowledge proofs, argues Brian Trunzo, chief growth officer at Succinct Labs.
items.author: Brian Trunzo

items.headline: The KIDS Act is way worse than digital carding — it is a mass surveillance system
items.subheadline: The fact that lawmakers are even contemplating a bill that would create a surveillance and censorship regime should be a wake-up call for everyone who values privacy and free expression, argues Electronic Frontier Foundation's India McKinney.
items.author: India McKinney

items.headline: Democratizing weather derivatives through tokenization could be blockchain industry’s most important real-world use case
items.subheadline: Main Street, which faces the most significant climate-related financial risk, currently lacks an avenue to hedge weather-related risks, argues CoinDesk’s Omkar Godbole.
items.author: Omkar Godbole

items.headline: Ballooning U.S. debt sends investors to bitcoin (BTC), gold to shelter from dollar devaluation: Crypto Daily
items.subheadline: The day ahead in crypto: July 27, 2026
items.author: Omkar Godbole

items.headline: Bitcoin options traders are dropping their hedges going into the Fed meeting
items.subheadline: The put/call ratio has fallen to about 0.52 from 0.76 in late June, and one-week downside protection has collapsed in price. The options market is positioned for a quiet week that contains an FOMC decision.
items.author: Shaurya Malwa

items.headline: Strategy (MSTR) bought back STRC shares, lifted cash reserves last week
items.subheadline: The company last week raised $525 million in cash via sales of its common stock.
items.author: Stephen Alpher

items.headline: Circle buys nearly 1,000 blockchain patents from IBM
items.subheadline: The portfolio covers blockchain technology, banking, insurance, and cloud security, though the financial terms of the deal were not disclosed.
items.author: Francisco Rodrigues

items.headline: Polymarket to challenge France’s nationwide website block
items.subheadline: France’s regulator has said the platform still promoted illegal gambling and cited loss, identity-check and market-manipulation risks.
items.author: Francisco Rodrigues

items.headline: Tokenized securities need competition, not gatekeepers
items.subheadline: Innovation thrives when investors have choices. For tokenized securities, Washington shouldn't pick winners before the market has a chance to learn what works, argues Patrick McHenry, vice chairman at Ondo Finance and former Chairman of the House Financial Services Committee.
items.author: Patrick McHenry

items.headline: MoneyGram's CEO says blockchain works best when customers don't know it's there
items.subheadline: In an interview with CoinDesk, MoneyGram CEO Anthony Soohoo said that their blockchain strategy has evolved from early experimentation into a broader effort to modernize the company's global payments infrastructure.
items.author: Margaux Nijkerk

items.headline: Live updates: Bitcoin gives up early gains, holds near $65,000 as AI stocks skid
items.subheadline: CoinEx's Jeff Ko sees bitcoin staying range-bound near $65,000 while retreating oil, a 4.7% 10-year yield and a week of mega-cap earnings set the tone.
items.author: Shaurya Malwa

items.headline: Robinhood Chain's real-world assets jump fivefold as tokenized stocks start trading in size
items.subheadline: The chain built to put equities onchain has tripled in size since mid-July, and a dozen tokenized stocks are now each clearing $500,000 a day. Real-world assets are growing fast, though memecoins and stablecoins still dominate the chain.
items.author: Shaurya Malwa

items.headline: North Korea arrests hackers accused of laundering stolen bank funds through crypto
items.subheadline: The group allegedly breached Central Bank systems, converted crypto to cash via Chinese brokers, and used small transfers to evade detection.
items.author: Francisco Rodrigues

items.headline: Russia’s largest bank Sberbank plans crypto trading infrastructure by December
items.subheadline: New regulations for crypto trading, custody, and settlement in Russia take effect Sept. 1, with requirements for licensed intermediaries applying from July 2027.
items.author: Francisco Rodrigues

items.headline: South Korea trade giant POSCO puts receivables onchain in tokenization test with LG
items.subheadline: POSCO International and LG CNS is tapping Injective network to tokenize live commercial invoices, another sign blockchain rails are moving deeper into corporate finance.
items.author: Krisztian Sandor

items.headline: Storj files for Chapter 11, extending a week of crypto failures. Token slides 16%
items.subheadline: The decentralized data storage company says operations continue and proposes that token holders take equity in the restructured business — an unusual arrangement in bankruptcy.
items.author: Shaurya Malwa

items.headline: Why the Coinbase CEO thinks pivoting from crypto to AI is a mistake
items.subheadline: The executive rejected the idea that the two sectors are in direct competition, framing blockchain as fundamental infrastructure for future automation.
items.author: Olivier Acuna

items.headline: Crypto Week Ahead
items.subheadline: Your look at what's coming in the week starting July 27.
items.author: Francisco Rodrigues

items.headline: Bitcoin holds firm as Hormuz hostilities pause, Fed prepares interest-rate decision: Crypto Markets Today
items.subheadline: Brent crude plunged 7% after the U.S. and Iran paused Strait of Hormuz strikes, lifting equities and DeFi tokens while bitcoin held near $65,000 ahead of a pivotal Fed decision Wednesday.
items.author: Oliver Knight

items.headline: Bitcoin ETFs post third straight weekly inflows despite $465 million in late-week losses
items.subheadline: The vast majority of the activity was concentrated in BlackRock’s IBIT product accounting for nearly $415 million of the outflows.
items.author: Jamie Crawley

items.headline: Crypto giant Galaxy sets up $5 million fund to future-proof Bitcoin security
items.subheadline: The company is backing developers to fix security blind spots before next-generation supercomputers become advanced enough to bypass blockchain protection.
items.author: Olivier Acuna

items.headline: Claude's Fable 5 just solved an 87-year-old math problem, and it matters for bitcoin
items.subheadline: Claude Fabel 5 disproved the Jacobian conjecture over the weekend, landing days after the capabilities of China's Kimi AI became the biggest force moving bitcoin markets.
items.author: Shaurya Malwa

items.headline: Live updates: Bitcoin holds near $66,000 as stocks claw back from big early decline
items.subheadline: Later on Wednesday, Alphabet's earnings should give a sign of whether the hundreds of billions going into AI is paying off.
items.author: Shaurya Malwa

items.headline: Balance stablecoin collapses 99% after $1 million exploit drains its bitcoin vaults
items.subheadline: An attacker fed the lending system a fake, abnormally low bitcoin price, liquidated vaults that should have been safe, and pocketed the difference in a single transaction.
items.author: Shaurya Malwa

items.headline: Arbitrum-based AFX Trade drained of $24 million after bridge keys compromised
items.subheadline: Security firms said the attacker used enough hot-validator signatures to approve a 24.15 million USDC withdrawal, while Arbitrum said its native bridge was not affected.
items.author: Shaurya Malwa

items.headline: Bitcoin, Ethereum-linked protocols lose $35 million in multiple attacks hours apart
items.subheadline: The attacks hit Verus, B² Network and other cross-chain systems, showing how compromised keys, upgrade powers and validation checks can empty protocols without breaking the underlying cryptography.
items.author: Shaurya Malwa

items.headline: Live markets: Bitcoin slides as stocks slump on Iran war expansion, AI spending concern
items.subheadline: Chipmaker Intel's revenue beat helped ease sentiment after a bruising session for tech stocks, with bitcoin holding near $65,000.
items.author: Shaurya Malwa

items.headline: Live updates: Bitcoin gives up gains, falls below $64,000 as stocks retreat
items.subheadline: Michael Saylor's Strategy — under continued pressure in this crypto bear market — released a new set of metrics to judge company performance.
items.author: Shaurya Malwa

items.headline: India orders takedown of Jack Dorsey’s bitcoin-linked messaging app Bitchat
items.subheadline: The order targets Bitchat, an offline Bluetooth mesh app built to relay encrypted messages and bitcoin transactions, as 'Cockroach Janta Party' protesters in Delhi use mesh tools to communicate through internet shutdowns.
items.author: Shaurya Malwa

items.headline: Europe is closing the door on offshore crypto, but it’s leaving the riskiest window open
items.subheadline: MiCA was never meant to address the giant crypto derivatives market. That could pose a serious problem, says Patrick Gruhn, founder and chief executive of Perpetuals.com.
items.author: Patrick Gruhn

items.headline: Europe led on crypto regulation. Now implementation must match ambition
items.author: Richard Teng

items.headline: Collateral, not yield, will decide which stablecoins win
items.subheadline: As yield-bearing stablecoins race toward a $50 billion market capitalization, the industry is optimizing for the wrong metric, argues Artem Tolkachev, chief RWA officer at Falcon Finance.
items.author: Artem Tolkachev

items.headline: Age verification is the surveillance nobody voted for
items.subheadline: KOSA and Chat Control both retreated on their most-criticized measures this week, but both kept mandatory age verification, the quiet mechanism that turns anonymous browsing into identified browsing for all of us, argues Billions CEO Evin McMullen.
items.author: Evin McMullen

items.headline: The UK has finally shown it’s serious about crypto
items.subheadline: Several recent regulatory steps indicate the UK might finally stop dragging its feet when it comes to crypto, argues Wirex CEO Chet Shah.
items.author: Chet Shah

items.headline: The Clarity Act isn't a ticket to sanctions evasion, actually
items.subheadline: The bill, as currently drafted, has the power to stop sanctions evasion at scale, argues Ari Redbord, global head of policy at TRM Labs.
items.author: Ari Redbord

items.headline: The privacy paradox of protecting kids online
items.subheadline: We don’t need to imagine the privacy pitfalls of age verification. They’ve been happening for years, argues Cardano Foundation CEO Frederik Gregaard.
items.author: Frederik Gregaard

items.headline: Goldman Sachs CEO backs Clarity Act despite banking industry's concerns over stablecoin rules
items.subheadline: The Goldman Sachs CEO said the crypto market structure bill would create a more stable regulatory framework, breaking with other major bank leaders who oppose key stablecoin provisions.
items.author: Helene Braun

items.headline: The SEC settles with Coinbase over its missing Gary Gensler texts
items.subheadline: Coinbase chief Brian Armstrong targeted the agency on social media, claiming the erased message chains point to a broader lack of government accountability.
items.author: Olivier Acuna

items.headline: Clarity Act expected to miss its window before Congress' summer break, leadership says
items.subheadline: The deadline to get the crypto market structure bill done before senators scatter will likely be missed, says Majority Leader Thune, though it may get a start before then.
items.author: Jesse Hamilton

items.headline: EU deploys a 21st sanction package against Russia that escalates bans on 14 crypto firms
items.subheadline: The EU's new sanctions packages includes the possibility of introducing a ban that would enable the EU to ban any transaction between an EU crypto provider and Russia.
items.author: Olivier Acuna

items.headline: Senate Dems should accept the victory they won on Trump's crypto limits: White House
items.subheadline: U.S. Senate Democrats got President Donald Trump to accept potential limits on his lucrative crypto dealings, but they say the Clarity Act's restrictions aren't enough.
items.author: Jesse Hamilton

items.headline: Europe's high regulatory bar could spark new crypto industry M&A wave
items.subheadline: As MiCA beds in and the U.K. finalizes its crypto framework, stringent regulation could spur mergers, acquisitions and closer ties with banks.
items.author: Jamie Crawley

items.headline: U.S. regulator warns prediction markets against cutting corners in event contracts
items.subheadline: The Commodity Futures Trading Commission again issued an advisory that signals firms have been straying into cookie-cutter self-certification.
items.author: Jesse Hamilton

items.headline: Ethereum news: Bitmine (BMNR) buys more as Tom Lee says ETH-BTC sends bullish signal
items.subheadline: The Ethereum treasury company added nearly 10,000 ETH while expanding its stock buyback, citing ether outperforming bitcoin is sending a bullish signal.
items.author: Krisztian Sandor

items.headline: Crypto is rewriting how Wall Street traders spend their weekends
items.subheadline: Around-the-clock crypto markets are forcing Wall Street to reevaluate one of its oldest assumptions: that weekends are for waiting.
items.author: Aoyon Ashraf

items.headline: BlackRock tokenization partner Securitize (SECZ) adds SEC investment adviser license amid institutional push
items.subheadline: The license broadens the BlackRock tokenization partner's offering as regulators weigh rules for onchain investment products.
items.author: Krisztian Sandor

items.headline: Nvidia forms 37-member AI security alliance without OpenAI, Anthropic or Google
items.subheadline: The chipmaker and 36 other companies say defenders need AI they can run themselves. Major AI players OpenAI, Anthropic and Google are not among them.
items.author: Shaurya Malwa

items.headline: Thailand's SEC alleges Bitkub concealed cyberattack that led to $50 million hack
items.subheadline: Bitkub was the victim of a cyberattack in May 2021, which led to hacks stealing 1.7 billion baht across 16 different digital assets.
items.author: Jamie Crawley

items.headline: Lido starts historic $16 billion migration to optimize Ethereum performance
items.subheadline: The liquid-staking giant is consolidating more than 8 million ether onto a lean validator architecture to drop overall network message traffic by nearly 30%.
items.author: Olivier Acuna

items.headline: Swiss crypto bank AMINA taps Cantor to explore public listing
items.subheadline: The Swiss bank is exploring multiple paths to the public markets, though discussions are ongoing and no final decision has been made.
items.author: Will Canny

items.headline: Fanatics buys regulated exchange in bid to grow prediction markets business
items.subheadline: The deal gives Fanatics control of its own prediction market infrastructure as event-based trading gains traction across sports, finance and crypto.
items.author: Helene Braun

items.headline: What are perps, anyway? Everything you need to know about crypto’s hottest trading instrument
items.subheadline: Perps, which launched on BitMEX in 2016, have become one of the most traded financial products in the world.
items.author: Oliver Knight

items.headline: Uphold reduces global headcount by 17% amid enterprise pivot
items.subheadline: The crypto trading platform said the layoffs reflect a strategic shift toward its fast-growing enterprise business.
items.author: Will Canny

items.headline: Crypto’s favorite $90 trillion trading product is coming to Wall Street, but big banks are taking it slow
items.subheadline: Regulated perpetual futures are officially landing in the U.S., but while agile trading firms and crypto exchanges race to capture massive retail demand, traditional Wall Street banks are holding back until liquidity, rules, and infrastructure mature.
items.author: Helene Braun

items.headline: Bitcoin (BTC) price may fall to $52,000 as demand remains elusive, Nansen analyst says
items.subheadline: BTC held near $65,000 even as Nvidia and AI stocks fell sharply. This week's Fed decision could determine whether bitcoin finally breaks higher or revisits June's lows, analysts said.
items.author: Krisztian Sandor

items.headline: Kalshi, Polymarket win pause against Minnesota's prediction market ban
items.subheadline: A federal judge ruled that Minnesota's law criminalizing prediction markets would probably violate the federal Commodity Exchange Act.
items.author: Nikhilesh De

items.headline: U.S. Senate puts off crypto Clarity Act for now as it focuses limited bandwidth elsewhere
items.subheadline: The majority leader is pursuing floor time for unrelated bills as the crypto industry waits for its policy effort to get its chance for votes.
items.author: Jesse Hamilton

items.headline: Bitcoin (BTC) price news: Price drops 2% after U.S. close while Korea’s Kospi plunges 10%
items.author: Omkar Godbole

items.headline: Bitcoin recovers from Asian session lows; Nasdaq futures remain under pressure
items.subheadline: It's a risk-off day. Still, bitcoin is holding better than Nasdaq and Asian equity markets.
items.author: Omkar Godbole
